newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK SPP, GAZPROM IN TALKS FOR PIPELINE JV.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK SPP, GAZPROM IN TALKS FOR PIPELINE JV.

text.p: Slovak state-owned monopoly gas distributor SPP s.p. said on Wednesday it was negotiating with Russian gas firm Gazprom on the creation of a joint venture to build and operate gas pipelines.

"Our company is negotiating with Gazprom on creating a joint-venture to build and manage gas pipelines carrying Russian gas to western consumers through Slovakia," Lubomir Rabay, SPP spokesman told Reuters.
"It should be something similar to what exists in Hungary, but in our case the Slovak side should have a majority stake."
Gazprom has a 50 percent stake in a joint-venture called Panrusgas with Hungarian oil and gas processing firm MOL holding the remaining 50 percent.
Rabay said the planned joint venture would have no influence on the current transfer of Russian gas through already existing pipelines.
"It will manage new pipelines, but this will first require new contracts between Gazprom and its western clients, which, as far as I know, have yet to be signed," Rabay said.
He declined to disclose any further details of the planned deal saying both partners have agreed to provide only limited information.
SPP is one of the most profitable Slovak companies, with its 1996 after-tax profit expected at some 8.862 billion crowns, on revenues totalling around 48 billion crowns.
Most of its revenues come from transit fees on Russian gas to western Europe, which last year totalled around 80 billion cubic metres.
The pipeline, which began operation in April 1971, serves about 10 major consumers in central and western Europe.
Gazprom pays for the transfer by supplying about four billion cubic metres of gas to Slovak consumers, which covers about two-thirds of domestic annual consumption.
